red_team_source.sole_material_defect: SS12 -- RangeConfigV3 (0.4.0) accepted unbounded d_min_bars (e.g. 200000); _Segment.slope() re-traversed the entire `closes` queue every bar -- O(d_min_bars)/bar. Measured: 20x increase in d_min_bars -> ~20.1x cost/bar (90.9us/bar at d_min=200, 1829us/bar at d_min=4000); extrapolated ~90ms/bar and ~8.9h at d_min_bars=200000 over 355,696 bars, over the declared 4h guarantee.
red_team_source.everything_else: RANGE V3 semantics (14 states/events, longitudinal segmentation, segment-local anchor, K/N, HBL-20, F7) verified independently PASS by Red Team -- untouched by this mandate (strict performance-only scope).

remedy.variant_chosen: A -- incremental OLS slope via sufficient statistics
remedy.variant_b_rejected_reason: No normative source (Statistician spec bf9f780) publishes any maximum for d_min_bars; the mandate explicitly forbids choosing an arbitrary cap just to pass the benchmark. Variant A resolves the defect with no cap needed.
remedy.method: For a fixed-size trailing window with equally-spaced integer x-positions 0..n-1: Sx(n)=n(n-1)/2 and Sxx(n)=n(n-1)(2n-1)/6 are closed-form functions of window size alone (O(1), no incremental tracking, zero precision-loss risk). Sy (sum of y) and Sxy (sum of position*y) are the only quantities maintained incrementally: growing phase = pure append at the current size; full phase = evict the value leaving position 0, shift is captured algebraically (Sxy_new = Sxy_old - Sy_old + y_evicted + (n-1)*y_new), then Sy_new = Sy_old - y_evicted + y_new. Final slope = (n*Sxy - Sx*Sy) / (n*Sxx - Sx*Sx), identical formula to the 0.4.0 batch computation. The bounded `closes` deque is retained solely to know which value is about to be evicted (O(1) peek) before each append.
remedy.verified_against_oracle: A naive full-recomputation oracle was checked at EVERY prefix (not just the final window) across 8 sequence shapes (constant/ramp-up/ramp-down/oscillating/duplicates/extremes/window-fill-exact/eviction-heavy) x 4 window sizes (1/2/12/20) -- worst absolute diff < 1e-6 in all cases; exact 0.0 diff observed on the full-engine oscillation parity fixture (see RANGE_V3_1_PARITY_REPORT.md SS1).
remedy.d_min_bars_configuration_limit: NONE -- any positive int is accepted and runs at O(1)/bar cost regardless of magnitude (verified directly at d_min_bars=96, 4000, and 200000).

ceo_amendment_d_min_bars_hardening.trigger: Found by VE during self-review (before any amendment was requested): RangeConfigV3 (0.4.0, inherited unchanged) never validated d_min_bars>0 -- a pre-existing gap, not introduced by the SS12 remedy. At d_min_bars=0, 0.4.0 stayed silent (slope()==0.0 forever, empty deque(maxlen=0)); 0.4.1 (before this amendment) raised an uncontracted IndexError from _SegmentV31.push_close(). Reported transparently in RANGE_V3_1_PARITY_REPORT.md SS5b before delivery.
ceo_amendment_d_min_bars_hardening.ceo_instruction: Do not finalize 0.4.1 delivery with d_min_bars=0 producing IndexError -- add fail-closed validation in the public config surface (int, >=1; reject 0/negative/float/bool/invalid types via a contractual exception, not IndexError); add public-API tests for -1/0/1/wrong-types; verify no invalid input mutates producer state; update the parity report and this manifest; treat as input-validation/fail-closed hardening, not a RANGE semantic change.
ceo_amendment_d_min_bars_hardening.fix: RangeConfigV31.__post_init__ (NEW override) calls super().__post_init__() first (0.4.0's K/N/w_atr/K<=N checks -- exact, unchanged), then rejects d_min_bars that is not a strict int (bool explicitly excluded despite being an int subtype in Python) or is <1, raising RangeSemanticContractErrorV3 (the SAME exception class already used for K>N and non-positive K/N/w_atr -- no new exception type invented).
ceo_amendment_d_min_bars_hardening.structural_guarantee: An invalid d_min_bars can never produce a RangeConfigV31 instance, so it can never reach _SegmentV31/RangeSemanticProducerV31/RangeSemanticEngineV31 -- the crash path is structurally unreachable, not merely caught downstream.
ceo_amendment_d_min_bars_hardening.benchmarks_restart_justification: Both in-flight benchmarks (canonical d_min_bars=96, adversarial d_min_bars=200000) use positive-integer d_min_bars values that were already valid and remain valid and behaviorally unchanged under the new check -- verified directly (both configs construct identically, identical range_spec_id()). The hardening gate is purely additive at config-construction time and does not touch the observe()/push_close()/slope() execution path exercised by either running benchmark.
